record.original_question: Let D be a planar domain. A sequence {zj } of points in D is said to be an interpolating sequence if whenever {αj } ∈ ℓ∞ there is a function F ∈ H ∞ (D) such that F (zj ) = αj , for all j. Suppose that the sequence {zj } has the property that for each j there is a function Fj ∈ H ∞ (D) such that Fj (zk ) = 0 if k 6= j, Fj (zj ) = 1 and kF k∞ ≤ C. Is {zj } necessarily an interpolating sequence? (P. W. Jones)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a planar domain and let $H^\infty(D)$ denote the Banach algebra of bounded holomorphic functions on $D$, equipped with the supremum norm $\|\cdot\|_\infty$. A sequence $\{z_j\}$ of distinct points in $D$ is called an interpolating sequence for $H^\infty(D)$ if for every bounded sequence $\{\alpha_j\} \in \ell^\infty$ there exists a function $F \in H^\infty(D)$ such that $F(z_j) = \alpha_j$ for all $j$.

Suppose that the sequence $\{z_j\} \subset D$ has the following weak (or "individual") interpolation property: there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that for each index $j$ there is a function $F_j \in H^\infty(D)$ with
$$F_j(z_j) = 1, \qquad F_j(z_k) = 0 \text{ for all } k \neq j, \qquad \|F_j\|_\infty \leq C.$$

Question: Must $\{z_j\}$ then be an interpolating sequence for $H^\infty(D)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a definitive resolution of P. W. Jones's question on whether the weak (individual) interpolation property with uniformly bounded peaking functions implies the full $\ell^\infty$ interpolation property for $H^\infty(D)$ on a general planar domain $D$. For the unit disk this is classical, but for arbitrary planar domains the problem is generally listed as an open problem in function-theory problem collections, and no published solution was located.

status_evidence.title: The constant of interpolation
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Peter Jones's interpolation constants for H^infinity, related to interpolating sequences on the disk and planar domains.
status_evidence.claim: Work on the H^infinity interpolation constant relates directly to Jones's question but does not resolve it for general planar domains.

status_evidence.title: VII Interpolating Sequences (Garnett, Bounded Analytic Functions)
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference on interpolating sequences for H^infinity, where weak vs. strong interpolation properties are discussed.
status_evidence.claim: The equivalence between weak and strong interpolation is classical on the disk but is not known to extend to arbitrary planar domains.
